data.name: Treachery in Beatdown City
data.detailed_description:
Prepare to take the streets back as three unlikely yet incredible heroes in this hybrid tactical beat-em-up where you’ll go up against not only the corrupt system, but fight off hordes of fascist cops, disorderly thugs, preppy cyclists, entitles joggers, affluent punks, ninjas, terrorists; and even ninja terrorists.



After the President Blake Orama is kidnapped by ninja terrorists and Mayor Mike Moneybags shuts down the police force, now-suspended police chief Antonio Santiago can sense something bigger is coming. He enlists the aid of his daughter Lisa and her two friends; Brad and Bruce, to set out to discover not only the truth; but also to find the root of the treachery in Beatdown City.



Will they save the president? You have to play to find out!

FEATURES:

  • Switch between 3 completely unique fighters - Lisa, an MMA fighter and Boxer, Bruce, a Jeet Kune Do/Capoeira specialist, and Brad, a former professional wrestler.
  • Choose from dozens of attacks to create strike combos, grapple combos, and strike and grapple-ombos!
  • Use a mix of real time and COMBO MENU based attacks to tackle your foes!
  • Inflict a huge number of Status Effects such as Stun, Burn and Bleed; and give yourself awesome buffs to turn the tide in your favor!
  • Fight against class based enemies, each with their own unique attack styles, behavior patterns and looks!
  • Nod your head to a timeless score by Inverse Phase, creator of such albums as Pretty Eight Machine and the Chipping of Isaac

reviews.review:
Treachery in Beatdown City takes the familiar concept of a retro street brawler and transforms it into something far more tactical than its pixel-art appearance initially suggests. Instead of relying on rapid button presses and straightforward combos, the game blends beat ’em up movement with menu-driven RPG combat, creating battles where planning is often more important than reflexes. Developed by NuChallenger and HurakanWorks and published by NuChallenger, it stands apart from conventional genre throwbacks by using nostalgia as its visual foundation while introducing a combat system with its own distinctive personality.

The story begins with an intentionally outrageous political crisis. President Blake Orama has been kidnapped by ninja terrorists, while Mayor Mike Moneybags responds to the situation in a manner that only makes Beatdown City more chaotic. Suspended police chief Antonio Santiago eventually turns to his daughter Lisa and her allies Bruce and Brad to investigate the increasingly bizarre situation. What follows is a journey through neighborhoods filled with criminals, aggressive citizens, corrupt personalities, ninjas, and other eccentric opponents. The kidnapping provides the central motivation, but much of the game's character comes from its smaller confrontations and satirical portrayal of urban society.

Combat represents its most unusual feature. Players can move their fighter around the battlefield much like they would in an old-fashioned brawler, but attacking involves opening a tactical menu and choosing individual techniques. This temporarily changes the pace from active movement to deliberate decision-making. Each action consumes resources, meaning that repeatedly choosing powerful attacks is not necessarily the smartest approach. Positioning, timing, resource management, enemy vulnerabilities, and the properties of individual techniques all influence the outcome.

The three protagonists also provide meaningful variety. Lisa is an MMA-oriented fighter whose repertoire incorporates boxing and versatile close-range techniques. Bruce combines Jeet Kune Do and Capoeira, giving him a distinctive martial arts approach, while Brad relies heavily on professional wrestling techniques and powerful grappling. Their differences encourage experimentation because some encounters naturally favor particular fighting styles. Switching characters and learning how their moves function is therefore an important part of mastering the game rather than merely a cosmetic choice.

A substantial collection of techniques gradually expands the tactical possibilities. Strikes and grapples can be arranged into combinations, allowing players to build sequences appropriate for different situations. Status conditions further complicate combat, with effects such as bleeding, burning, and stunning providing alternatives to straightforward damage. Buffs and other beneficial conditions can similarly improve a fighter's effectiveness. These mechanics make seemingly modest attacks valuable when they establish opportunities for stronger follow-ups.

Enemy encounters reinforce the puzzle-like nature of the combat. Beatdown City is populated by numerous enemy types with different abilities and behavioral patterns. Some encounters reward aggression, while others require careful management of positioning and resources. The roster of adversaries also contributes significantly to the comedy, presenting an intentionally exaggerated collection of street-level troublemakers, authority figures, social stereotypes, and increasingly absurd threats. Recurring rivals and more demanding confrontations add challenge, although familiarity with the systems can eventually make certain battles easier to predict.

The writing is unusually prominent for this type of game. Conversations regularly precede fights, providing context for confrontations and giving enemies recognizable personalities rather than reducing them to interchangeable targets. The humor frequently uses social and political satire, addressing subjects such as privilege, prejudice, corruption, online culture, and obnoxious public behavior. Its comedy can be deliberately confrontational, so its effectiveness will depend considerably on the player's taste. Nevertheless, the strong authorial voice helps prevent the experience from feeling like another generic recreation of an arcade-era brawler.

Its visual presentation embraces pixel art while giving characters enough expressive animation to complement the comedic writing. Streets, interiors, fighters, and enemies maintain a colorful retro atmosphere without overwhelming the screen with unnecessary detail. Wrestling maneuvers and martial arts techniques are particularly entertaining when translated into this deliberately old-fashioned graphical style. The energetic soundtrack by Inverse Phase fits naturally alongside the visuals and contributes substantially to the feeling of playing an unusual game inspired by an earlier era.

The biggest potential obstacle is pacing. Anyone expecting nonstop real-time fighting may find the constant transition between movement and tactical menus initially awkward. Combat becomes much more enjoyable after understanding how resources, status effects, positioning, and combinations interact, but it never becomes a traditional button-mashing brawler. Repeated enemy types can also make later encounters feel somewhat routine once effective strategies have been discovered. The deliberate structure gives the game strategic depth, but it inevitably sacrifices some of the immediate momentum associated with classic arcade fighting.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable advantage. The game is officially Steam Deck Verified, with its core functionality working through the handheld's controls and its interface remaining usable on the smaller display. Controller prompts and general navigation are appropriately supported, while the game can run using settings suitable for the device. Its viewpoint and methodical pacing also translate naturally to portable play, although demanding visual settings can still make sensible performance adjustments worthwhile for players prioritizing battery life or consistent performance.

Ultimately, Treachery in Beatdown City succeeds by refusing to imitate classic beat ’em ups too closely. Its mixture of tactical RPG mechanics, street fighting, character-specific abilities, resource management, status effects, satire, and retro presentation gives it an identity that is difficult to confuse with anything else. The slower combat rhythm and occasional repetition will not appeal to everyone, but players who enjoy analyzing encounters and constructing effective attack combinations will find considerable depth beneath the intentionally simple exterior. It is a creative genre experiment with enough humor and mechanical personality to remain memorable long after its novelty has worn off.

Rating: 7/10

Mínimos:

  • Processador: Intel Core 2 Duo 1.8Ghz or equivalent
  • Memória: 3 GB de RAM

  • Espaço no disco: Requer 200 MB de espaço livre
